The official Postmark sources say the 10,000-email tier is the entry point, but dedicated IPs are reserved for much higher volumes. Third-party comparison sites disagree on that last point.

**Plans:** Postmark's support center says it offers several monthly plans starting at 10,000 emails/month. For volumes above that, you need to get in touch to discuss high-volume tiers.

**Dedicated IPs (official):** Postmark lists dedicated IPs as an add-on starting at $50/month per IP. The pricing page adds that they are available to customers sending 300,000+ emails/month and only available on Pro plans or higher.

**Conflict:** Several Courier.com comparison pages say customers sending up to 300,000 emails monthly can use a dedicated IP address with an additional cost of $50 per month. That reads as the opposite of Postmark's own threshold, so I'd treat the official page as authoritative and confirm with Postmark before relying on the Courier version. Note too that those comparison pages date from different years (2025 and 2026 editions appear), so they may be out of date.

**Bottom line:** A 10,000-email/month account is on a standard plan and, per Postmark's own page, would not qualify for a dedicated IP unless it moves to a Pro tier and reaches the 300,000-email threshold.

## Pricing

**Resend** ([pricing](https://resend.com/pricing.md), [docs](https://resend.com/docs/knowledge-base/what-is-resend-pricing.md))
- Free is $0/month for 3,000 emails. One source says it's capped at 100 emails per day.
- Pro is $20/month for 50,000 emails. The docs also show a $35/month tier for 100,000 emails.
- Overage is about $0.90 per 1,000 emails.
- Third-party guides list Scale at about $90/month for 100,000 emails. I couldn't confirm that.
- A dedicated IP is a $30/month add-on. Sources disagree on the volume it requires.

**Postmark** ([pricing](https://postmarkapp.com/pricing.txt), [support](https://postmarkapp.com/support/article/1107-how-does-monthly-pricing-work))
- Plans start at 10,000 emails/month. I couldn't retrieve the entry price or overage rates, so check those.
- A dedicated IP costs $50/month per IP. Postmark's page says it requires 300,000+ emails/month and a Pro plan or higher. Some third-party comparison pages state this differently, so I'd trust Postmark's own page.

## Deliverability features
I couldn't retrieve either vendor's feature list this session, so what follows is background knowledge, not something I just looked up.
- **Postmark** is known for strict anti-spam vetting at signup. It also separates transactional and broadcast traffic into different message streams. Its reputation for inbox placement and delivery speed is among the best for transactional mail.
- **Resend** offers DKIM/SPF setup, a modern API and good developer experience. It has a shorter track record on deliverability.

## Recommendation
**Postmark** is my pick if deliverability matters most. That includes password resets, receipts and login codes, where a delayed or missed email costs you. Its stricter vetting protects sender reputation.

**Resend** is the better pick if you want a free tier, a lower entry cost at 50k+ emails, and a modern developer experience, for example with React Email templates.
